illustrationLicensing.rationale: A CC license grants copyright permissions; purely AI-generated output likely lacks the human authorship copyright requires (US Copyright Office: Zarya of the Dawn, Thaler). Marking CC0 is safe either way -- it claims nothing false if the images are uncopyrightable, and is a deliberate dedication if they are not. Avoids binding readers to an unenforceable ShareAlike obligation.
illustrationLicensing.requires: per-asset provenance sidecar (generator, model, prompt, date, sha256); prompts must avoid living artists, brands, and recognizable characters; generator ToS reviewed per asset.

notes.MAJOR_FINDING_no_payoffs: THE headline finding of the HL-C11 fan-out. Across latin (36 ch), hindi (30), tamil (27) — the three largest tracks reported so far — essentially NO chapter has a schema-v2 terminal consolidation lesson. Latin has exactly one `practice` lesson across 36 chapters and no practice-mix at all. Hindi's two practice lessons are schema v1 and outside the curriculum path. Tamil has none. So payoffs fall back to 'last lesson by sequence', which is frequently an etymology, culture, or script-writing lesson — the reader traces a root or forms a letter rather than performing a usable exchange. Every representativeness failure reported so far sits on exactly such a chapter. The ledger is honestly DOCUMENTING that the corpus does not yet have chapter payoffs, which is precisely the gap the Step-by-Step goal exists to close. Persian/Urdu are the exception and the quality bar: real `practice` lessons minting *-DIALOGUE-* atoms.

Correct call. 123 of 375 chapters have drivable prefix 0 - you cannot even START them by ear.
notes.atomClassProblem: SYSTEMATIC CAUSE of nearly every representativeness failure, identified independently by the persian/urdu and arabic/malayalam agents. Word lessons introduce *-SCRIPT-* and *-ETYMON-* atoms (FA-SCRIPT-KHUB, UR-CROSSLINGUAL-KHUDA-HAFIZ-SPELLING, ...) that a consolidating DIALOGUE never re-exercises - because you cannot 'perform' an etymon in a spoken exchange. So the denominator counts atom classes the payoff is structurally incapable of assessing. Persian ch4/ch5 and Urdu ch4/ch5 all fail for exactly this reason, as do Arabic ch3 (0.11) and ch4 (0.12). This is a METRIC DESIGN question, not per-chapter content debt: either weight atom classes differently in the denominator, or require a different check for script/etymon coverage (e.g. a writing companion or a recall prompt rather than the dialogue).
notes.russianIsTheWorstTrack: Russian is the consistent outlier on BOTH independent measurements: 9% drivable (2 voice/15 sight/5 pen, zero lessons reachable by ear) AND 0.20 representativeness on its single authorable chapter. Only 6 of 22 lessons are schema v2, its practice-mix lessons are schema v1 so the payoff fell back to a cross-language etymology lesson, and ch2 has no book-generation target. Two unrelated metrics agreeing means this is a real track-health problem, not measurement noise. Worth a dedicated remediation pass.

notes.penLiftsSemantics: KEY SEMANTIC established by #9976, do not erode: `penLifts` absent means NOT VERIFIED, never NONE, and it must NEVER be inferred from strokeOrder.length. A strokeOrder list names a letter's PARTS in writing order; it has never counted pen-down runs. Three named parts can be three strokes OR one continuous stroke whose parts merely have names - Tamil ma is the latter.

notes.MEASUREMENT_BUG_orderChapterLessons: P0 CORRECTION to numbers I already reported. HL-C14 orderChapterLessons sorts a chapter by `sequence` with null last, tie-broken by id. notes.REPRESENTATIVENESS_IS_NEARLY_VACUOUS: MY DESIGN ERROR, found by HL-C24. I specced payoff representativeness in HL05 and called it 'the rule that carries the weight'. It does not. All 36 Latin chapters measured 100% BEFORE and AFTER adding real payoff lessons, because a chapter's last teaching lesson cumulatively practises everything the chapter introduced. The metric answers 'does the payoff TOUCH the chapter's material', never 'can the reader DO something'. It discriminates only where a terminal lesson happens to be narrow (arabic ch3 0.11, hindi ch2 0.17, spanish ch3 0.25) - so what it actually measures is HOW CUMULATIVE a track's terminal lessons are, not payoff quality. Combined with HL-C31 (ETYMON/SCRIPT atoms in the denominator), the rule needs redesign before HL-C03 builds it. The honest signal HL-C24 found: chapters ending on a lesson WRITTEN to be a payoff, 1 of 36 -> 5 of 36 for Latin.
notes.HL_C25_IS_EDGES_NOT_LESSONS: SCOPING INSIGHT for the biggest remaining item. Latin's prerequisite chain is a LINE, not a tree - lessons name one or two prerequisites each - so material taught in a SIBLING branch is invisible to a payoff even though the reader demonstrably learned it. Latin ch36 could not see the bonus-phrase atoms until explicit prerequisite edges were authored. So HL-C25 is not 'write 350 lessons', it is 'AUTHOR PREREQUISITE EDGES, THEN write lessons'. Budget for the edges or every payoff silently shrinks to whatever its one ancestor line happened to carry.
notes.TABLES_ARE_THE_LEVER: PROVEN by HL-C32. Russian: 15 of 15 sight lessons tripped `wide-table`, ZERO tripped script-block. The internal proof is decisive: RU-C01-privet and RU-C01-zdravstvuyte carry the SAME 'Across the family' content as PROSE and were the track's only two voice lessons. Same content, two formattings, two modalities. Converting tables to prose took Russian 9% -> 73% drivable with zero content loss. Corpus-wide, 271 of the 337 remaining sight lessons trip wide-table and NOTHING ELSE - spanish 57, german 33, portuguese 32, french 29, italian 29, arabic 14, tamil 14. HL-C17 is the single largest modality lever in the corpus and Russian is the worked example.

notes.representativenessIsOftenSchemaDebt: REFRAME. The low representativeness scores (arabic ch3 0.11/ch4 0.13, hindi ch2 0.17, spanish ch3 0.25) are largely NOT 'this chapter has no payoff'. The chapter's REAL consolidation lesson exists but is schema v1, so the ledger had to point at a schema-v2 stand-in (an etymology or writing lesson). A ONE-LESSON schema-v2 migration fixes each - HL-C32 did exactly that for RU-C02-practice and moved ch2 from 0.20 to 0.67. That is far cheaper than authoring new payoffs.
notes.TWO_EDITIONS_NOT_ONE_COMPROMISED_BOOK: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-06, corrects an instinct of mine. The BOOK is the complete standalone artifact and keeps ALL writing content - it must never be thinned to protect the drivability metric. A DICTATION-FRIENDLY DRIVING EDITION comes later as a separate output view over the same canonical source, omitting what a driver cannot do. I had proposed contorting the book (block-level modality) so interspersed writing would not hurt drivability; that was the wrong trade. Block-level modality is still worth having, but for a better reason: it lets the future driving edition skip just the writing SEGMENT instead of dropping the whole lesson, which today costs a commuter every lesson containing any pen content.
notes.DRIVING_EDITION_IS_PREFIX_SHAPED: CRITICAL for HL-C43. You CANNOT build the driving edition by filtering `drivable`. 708 lessons are ear-only but only 551 are REACHABLE - 157 sit behind a blocker inside their own chapter. The filter is PREFIX-shaped, not set-shaped: the edition must TRUNCATE chapters, not select lessons. The manifest emits `drivableLessonIds` in authored order precisely so the renderer does not re-derive this and get it wrong. Also: 121 of 375 chapters cannot be STARTED at all, usually one pen/script lesson sitting first - they are not inaudible, they are front-loaded. That is what makes HL-C41's block-level modality load-bearing rather than nice-to-have: without it the driving edition loses a third of the corpus to opening segments.

notes.SCALE_TEST_CHINESE_RESULT:
THE ANSWER to 'does this scale to all languages': the STRUCTURE scales, the METHOD does not.
HELD: the lesson schema carried tone with ZERO frontmatter change (sounds: [tone-3, tone-sandhi-third], exactly like Persian's sounds: [rtl, long-a]). Just-in-time script introduction transferred intact.
BROKE 1 - the DATA layer. Letter.tone can only label a glyph. It cannot express the tone INVENTORY (contour 214 belongs to the sound system, not to any character) nor SANDHI, which changes a syllable's pitch because of the syllable AFTER it while the characters and printed pinyin stay identical. ni hao is spoken ni2 hao3; a learner trusting the page mispronounces the commonest greeting. It is a fact about a SEQUENCE and there is no Letter to hang it on. Added ScriptData.tones + ScriptData.toneSandhi.
BROKE 2 - HL00 walks word->letter (2 levels). Chinese has word->character->component (3). No correct answer to 'which level is letter': characters alone leave shapes unmemorable, components alone leave you unable to speak. Sharper: for Chinese 'the letters in this word' and 'the word, taken apart' are THE SAME ANALYSIS - 女+子 is both decomposition and memory hook. Every other track separates script from etymology BECAUSE letters carry no meaning.
BROKE 3, THE HEADLINE - the cousin web does not transfer at all. No shared ancestry, so HL00's engine has no fuel. No cognate was invented. Character composition substitutes but is WEAKER in a precise way: a cousin web anchors to knowledge the reader ALREADY HAS; a component gloss anchors to knowledge acquired IN THE SAME BREATH (女 means nothing until this course says so). It is also less reliable - 好 as woman+child is a TRADITIONAL GLOSS, not settled palaeography, and ~80% of characters are phono-semantic with sound components opaque after 3,000 years. bridges: [] on purpose.
notes.latentGap_lettersInThisWord_blockType: Schema v2 has NO block type for '## The letters in this word' - the heading HL00 specifies for inline script teaching. It occurs 240 times, all in schema-v1 lessons. Migrating any of those tracks to v2 will hit this.
notes.SCALE_TEST_VERDICT:
CHINESE AND JAPANESE AGREE. The STRUCTURE scales; the signature METHOD does not.
HELD in both: the lesson schema needed no frontmatter change (tone rode `sounds:` exactly like Persian's rtl; Japanese's multiple kanji readings rode `Letter.sound` as a free string). Just-in-time script introduction survives once 'letters' reads as 'the writing this word needs' - konnichiwa brings kana, nihongo brings kanji, koohii brings katakana, each on the word that forces it.
BROKE in both, same place: the DATA layer. Chinese - Letter.tone cannot express a tone inventory or sandhi (a property of a SEQUENCE, no Letter to hang it on). Japanese - HL01's Script is ONE STRING per track and uncoveredGlyphs validates against exactly one inventory, so three writing systems had to be merged into one file with a per-sign `role`, encoding a three-way distinction in a naming convention.
BROKE, THE HEADLINE: the cousin web does not transfer. Chinese has no shared ancestry at all and substitutes character composition, which is weaker in a precise way (anchors to knowledge acquired IN THE SAME BREATH rather than knowledge already owned). Japanese PARTIALLY redirects via Sino-Japanese, internal etymology, and shared borrowings - but exactly ONE of eight lessons produced an English cousin, and through a shared loan (koohii/coffee, both from Arabic qahwa) rather than shared descent.
THE TWO SECRETLY INDO-EUROPEAN PARTS OF HL00: (1) the Grounding section assumes every track has a deep root the reader owns through English; (2) the one-script-per-track rule.
notes.xelatexIsActuallyAvailable: DISCREPANCY worth acting on: the Japanese agent INSTALLED XeLaTeX and built its book (17 pages, 0 overfull, 0 missing glyphs, 1 underfull). The Chinese agent reported XeLaTeX unavailable and shipped with its first compile UNVERIFIED. So the capability exists and the Chinese book can and should be verified the same way.
notes.BOOK_VOICE_WHAT_A_RENDERER_CANNOT_FIX:
HL-C38 fixed the scaffolding (1,438 [PAUSE] + 1,411 [YOU SAY] gone, block headings renamed, appendix moved to backmatter in 17 books, repo links removed, 20 prefaces rewritten, 20 READMEs de-jargoned) and its verdict is that ch20-lo-siento now reads like a language book. FOUR things remain that a renderer change cannot fix, all chapter-level STRUCTURE:
1. Every lesson has the identical five-block skeleton, 1,096 times. Invisible in a one-lesson chapter, very visible in a six-lesson one.
2. Recall answers sit in parentheses immediately after their questions - correct for a spoken script, wrong on a page where the eye lands on the answer first.
3. NO CONNECTIVE TISSUE between sections. A many-lesson chapter reads as a LIST OF WORDS, not a chapter with an argument. This is the sharpest of the four and the real difference between a book and a glossary.
4. 'Your turn' / 'Before you move on' repeat once per lesson.
These need an owner decision - they are chapter-level authoring changes, not rendering.

durableNotes.why: Committed to the repo so a FRESH session (spawned by a durable Routine) can resume without this session's scratchpad, which is session-scoped and unreachable from a new one.
durableNotes.rateLimit: GitHub API rate limit was exceeded by aggressive polling. A durable loop MUST poll sparingly: at most one PR-state sweep per firing, and prefer `git ls-remote` over API calls where possible.
durableNotes.blockerLanded: HL-C50 (PR #9988) makes corpus pins DERIVED, so adding a track or splitting a lesson no longer edits any test file. That was the cause of 5-of-9 branch conflicts. Land it before resuming parallel work.
durableNotes.conflictPolicy: Doc conflicts (BACKLOG.md, CHANGELOG.md, README.md) are append-only: resolve by keeping BOTH sides. Non-doc conflicts need real review.
durableNotes.parallelPolicy: Fan out freely on PER-TRACK files (lessons/, chapters.json, per-track CHANGELOG) - the 20-track fan-out produced zero conflicts. SERIALIZE anything touching core/languages.json, core/book-generation.json, or shared test files.
durableNotes.agentBriefingRule: Agents branch from origin/main and see ONLY merged state. Always say which referenced work is merged vs in flight, and require BOTH test suites (human-language-data AND language-ladder) before pushing.
